clue.text: Painter refusing to work in inclement weather?

definitions.meaning: Franz Xaver ... was a nineteenth-century German court portraitist

definitions.text: refusing to work in inclement weather?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, someone who stops (halts) when the cold season comes

explanation.surface: An artist who downs brushes whenever the weather turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: split the name into a cold season and one who halts, and it describes a fair-weather worker.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter is named literally; the second reading imagines a person who calls a stop to work during the cold months.

clue.text: Turned green and appeared injured but sounded chirpy

indicators.note: turned around, so the word for green runs backwards

parts.note: raw means inexperienced, green
bled means lost blood, as an injured person does

explanation.surface: Someone went pale, seemed hurt, yet sang cheerfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned green' suggests nausea; it reverses RAW to WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Warbling is how songbirds trill, so singing like a bird.

clue.text: The drifter is certainly not crazy

parts.note: no is the flat refusal
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: Insisting a wanderer is perfectly sane.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad wanders from place to place without a settled home.

clue.text: Sees Latin translation as most important

indicators.note: a translation turns words into new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student deciding Latin translation matters above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges SEES and LATIN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is indispensable, of the highest priority.

clue.text: Greet in icy fashion

parts.note: a word for salute or call out to that also names frozen pellets falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Welcoming someone coldly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue pretends to describe a frosty welcome; really it is one word for both a greeting and frozen rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to call out a greeting, and hail is also ice falling in pellets.

clue.text: Decline to cause the sovereign distress

parts.note: a sovereign is a gold pound coin, and L is the pound sign
anguish is acute distress

explanation.surface: Refusing to upset the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' looks like the monarch, but it is the old British gold pound coin, and L (libra) abbreviates the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to weaken or fade, to decline in health.

clue.text: Dodge nowadays accepted by the first wife

indicators.note: the first wife's name takes in the other piece

parts.note: Eve, Adam's wife in Genesis
AD, anno Domini, the present era

explanation.surface: A modern dodge that Eve was willing to go along with.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to avoid or sidestep.

clue.text: An A for apprenticeship

definitions.meaning: 'an' and 'a' are the indefinite words of grammar placed before nouns
a period of training with a firm of solicitors or accountants under a formal contract

explanation.surface: Top marks awarded for an apprentice's work.
explanation.walkthrough: An articled clerk trains in a law firm under a contract, the noun used in the plural for that training.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls 'a' and 'an' indefinite determiners, and trainee lawyers serve under a training contract with the same name.

clue.text: Richly ornamental lid for make-up

indicators.note: make-up means composition, so the letters are made up into a new word

explanation.surface: An ornate eyelid painted for a cosmetic look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lid' and 'make-up' suggest eye cosmetics; 'make-up' rearranges LIDFOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A florid style is over-elaborate and flowery, heavily decorated.

clue.text: Religious settlement, on a note of forgiveness

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a mission is a station set up by missionaries

explanation.surface: A church outpost founded on a message of pardon.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission of sins is their pardon, a standard theological synonym for absolution.

clue.text: The days of Browning's nostalgia

parts.note: Robert Browning's Home-Thoughts, from Abroad opens by longing to be in England in a particular spring month

explanation.surface: A literary question about when the poet Browning felt homesick.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem begins 'Oh, to be in England / Now that ...'s there', naming the month the exiled poet pines for.
explanation.definitionFit: The month is the thirty-day spell the poem's speaker yearns to spend back home.

clue.text: The language of youth in love

parts.note: a lad is a young man
love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Asking what tongue young people speak when smitten.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring 'love' means zero, which crosswords render as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladino is the Judaeo-Spanish tongue of Sephardic Jews, so it is a language.

clue.text: A stretch of water that's quite unrivalled

definitions.meaning: the largest of North America's Great Lakes, on the US-Canada border
better than all others, without equal

explanation.surface: A body of water that has no rival anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The great lake carries this name, and the adjective means higher in quality than any competitor.

clue.text: A capital naturalist

definitions.meaning: the capital city of Australia's Northern Territory
Charles ..., the biologist of natural selection

explanation.surface: Praise for an excellent student of nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like an adjective meaning excellent qualifying 'naturalist'; it is a noun, a seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a city in northern Australia and the Victorian scientist of evolution bear this name.

clue.text: Ringing to storm about Oriental issue

indicators.note: the raging word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to rant is to storm, raging loudly
E, east, the Orient
a son is a person's issue, offspring

explanation.surface: Someone shouting angrily on the phone about an Eastern matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ESON inside RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant sound is full and echoing, reverberating.

clue.text: Attacked a fool, and suffered for it

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person
ailed means was unwell, suffered

explanation.surface: Someone set upon a fool and paid for it with pain afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to set upon violently, so the past tense matches set upon.

clue.text: Set against a lengthy party

parts.note: long means lengthy
a side is one party in a dispute or game

explanation.surface: Opposed to a political party that goes on far too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set against' looks like opposed; it means positioned next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed beside something is set next to it, so next to it in position.

clue.text: Labour on for survival

parts.note: the Labour party stands on the political left
over can mean on, as on top of

explanation.surface: A Labour Party slogan on survival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' is the British political party of the left. 'survival' is a noun for a relic that survives from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A survival is a thing that remains from an earlier time, a remnant.

clue.text: He'd excuse a rating doing the crossword

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a naval rating
a solver is someone working out puzzle answers

explanation.surface: A forgiving officer lets off a sailor caught doing the crossword on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'rating' is an ordinary sailor; crosswords use AB, able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: One who pardons or remits sins is someone who would excuse, an agent noun matching 'He'd excuse'.

clue.text: Stop men with guns sticking up others

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, gunners
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Armed men holding up other people at gunpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticking up' reads like a hold-up, but it turns RA to AR in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest is to halt something's progress, bring it to a stop.

clue.text: Felons, were at one time finally dependent on them

definitions.text: Felons, were at one time finally dependent on them

parts.words: Felons, were at one time finally dependent on them
parts.note: in the days of capital punishment, condemned criminals ended their lives hanging from ropes tied in running loops

explanation.surface: A remark that criminals once relied on something in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dependent' is literal: the felons were left hanging, and 'finally' because it was the end of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangman's ropes knotted in loops were what convicts once literally hung from at execution.

clue.text: The most hackneyed way to frame anecdotes

indicators.note: the first piece sits around the second like a frame

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
tales are anecdotes, stories

explanation.surface: A writer asks for the most clichéd way of telling stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' is the street abbreviation; the frame splits it, one letter each side of the stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalest means most trite, most overused.

clue.text: Give a face-lift, but never to a model

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Advice to a cosmetic surgeon never to operate on a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a fashion model, but it is a verb, to shape: rearrange NEVERTOA.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a building a face-lift means restoring or redecorating it to look new.

clue.text: A composer must have exceptional drive

indicators.note: unusual, out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A great composer needs remarkable ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptional' rearranges DRIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer.

clue.text: A girl getting a little evening bag at half-price

indicators.note: only a small part of the words is taken, the letters within the phrase

explanation.surface: A girl picks up a small evening bag in a half-price sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'bag at half': drop the B and the letters after HA.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is a woman's given name, as in the novelist Christie.

clue.text: Use a comb and occasion some irritation

definitions.meaning: to comb wool or hair to raise its fibres

explanation.surface: Combing someone's hair while getting on their nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to tease is to backcomb hair or card wool, and to provoke or annoy.

clue.text: Poles taking a quiet break

parts.note: S and N, the south and north poles
P, piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: Polish people taking a quiet holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a sudden break, as of a twig.

clue.text: The Spaniard when older has no need of one

indicators.note: doing without signals the letter is taken out

parts.note: senior means older in years
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman, once he has aged, no longer needs something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no need of' removes I (one) from SENIOR, leaving the Spanish word for Mr.
explanation.definitionFit: Senor is the Spanish title for a man, used to address any gentleman of Spain.

clue.text: Few show support

parts.note: V, the Roman five, stands for a small number
indicate means point out, show

explanation.surface: Only a handful turn out to demonstrate their backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Few' is a loose call for V, five, a small number in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate is to justify or uphold a claim, so it backs it.

clue.text: Reformed miser — now doctor

indicators.note: a reformed character has changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the present is the time now

explanation.surface: A former miser who has turned over a new leaf and become a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' turns MISER into MISRE. 'Doctor' looks like a noun, but is the verb, to falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor figures is to falsify them, giving a false account.
